skill.name: Executor Shutdown and Resource Cleanup
skill.description: Signal an Executor to free resources after pending futures complete, with optional cancellation of unstarted futures. Use when you are done submitting tasks and want to ensure clean resource release.
skill.skill_body:
Call executor.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False) to cleanly terminate the executor. Set wait=True to block until all pending futures complete. Set cancel_futures=True to cancel any futures that have not yet started execution. After shutdown, any calls to submit() or map() will raise RuntimeError.

## Objective

Cleanly terminate an Executor and release its resources
## Applicable Signals

- Completion of task submission loop
- End of executor usage scope
- Need to free thread or process pool resources

## Contraindications

- Do not call if you still need to submit new tasks
- Do not call if you want to keep the executor alive for future use
- Do not rely on shutdown to interrupt already-running futures

## Intervention Moves

- Call shutdown(wait=True) to block until pending futures complete
- Call shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True) to cancel unstarted futures and free resources immediately
- Use within a context manager (with statement) to ensure automatic cleanup

## Constraints

- After shutdown is called, submit() and map() will raise RuntimeError
- Completed or running futures will not be cancelled regardless of cancel_futures value
- If wait=False, shutdown returns immediately but resources may not be freed until pending futures complete

## Cautions

- Setting cancel_futures=True only cancels futures that have not started; running futures continue to completion
- Blocking on wait=True may cause the caller to wait indefinitely if a future hangs

## Output Contract

- Executor resources are freed
- All pending futures complete or are cancelled
- Subsequent submit() or map() calls raise RuntimeError
